subject: Sponsor embed options, closed captions workflow, and audio rights
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmeevents.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Webinar sponsor embed + captions questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the invite — excited to sponsor the June webinar. A couple of quick technical/legal questions from our side so we can coordinate with our marketing ops team: 

- We want to embed a live player on our marketing site during the event (iframe preferred). Is ON24/Zoom embeddable by us, and do you have a recommended iframe + security pattern (postMessage or tokenized URL)?
- We need closed captions (SRT or VTT) delivered within 30 minutes of the event end. Do you provide a live captions stream or just post-event files? Any preferred vendor integrations (e.g., Rev, 3Play)?
- We plan to cut a 30s promo clip and repurpose the audio for paid social. What language do you require in the sponsor SOW re: audio reuse and talent releases? Can we get a short affirmative in writing?

Attaching the draft SOW we use for sponsors (Acme_SOW_v2.pdf).

Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Head of Partnerships, Acme Events
oliver.hayes@acmeevents.com
+sponsor@acmeevents.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmeevents.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Webinar sponsor embed + captions questions

Thanks, Oliver — great questions. Looping in Ben (platform/ops) and Marissa (partner ops) to confirm the implementation details and legal/creative next steps. High-level answers below and a proposed action list so we have clear owners: 

Short answers: 
- Embed: We support iframe embedding for our hosted ON24 streams and for our Zoom-based webinars when using our player embed. We issue time-limited, tokenized embed URLs — recommended pattern: our embed URL (player.redwood.ai/embed) plus a short-lived JWT (TTL 10 minutes) and postMessage to surface controls. For your web team we can provide a sample snippet.
- Captions: We offer two flows: live captions (auto-generated, lower accuracy) and post-event human-refined SRT/VTT. For guaranteed quality (and within your 30-min SLA) the typical flow is human transcription (Rev) + expedited turnaround — ops will confirm feasibility for the requested window.
- Audio reuse/rights: We require sponsor SOW to include permission for Redwood to grant a one-time clip license to the sponsor for marketing use (30s clip, non-exclusive, worldwide, 2-year term). Legal prefers a short clause in the SOW; Marissa — can you confirm final wording?

Action items (owners):
1) Ben: confirm iframe token pattern + provide encoder/RTMP constraints and whether we can rotate tokens client-side for embed. Also share a credentials stub we can send to Acme to point their player at our stream. (Due: 2026-05-13 EOD)
2) Ben: confirm caption workflow (live vs human) and whether we can guarantee SRT delivery within 30 minutes. If not, propose alternatives (VTT live + human SRT T+4h).
3) Marissa: confirm SOW language for audio reuse and whether we need signed talent releases from panelists.
4) Chloe: provide sample iframe snippet + privacy/reg notice text for Acme’s landing page.

Ben/Marissa — please reply with the technical/contract snippets and attach any creds we need to hand to Acme. Oliver — I’ll follow up with a simple mutual action plan once we have the bits.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Field Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmeevents.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Webinar sponsor embed + captions questions

Chloe — answered inline, and attaching the encoder creds stub.

Embed/encoder notes:
- We can issue a time-limited embed JWT as you suggested. TTL 600s (10m) is default; if Acme needs longer page-load windows we can sign an intermediate token for their CDN (let us know).
- RTMP specifics: bitrate cap 6 Mbps, keyframe every 2s, H.264 baseline/main. We support SRT/RTMP ingest; for iframe embed we proxy the HLS from our CDN.
- Token rotation: recommend server-side rotation via short-lived JWTs and a refresh endpoint. If Acme wants client-side refresh we can provide a small JS helper (see snippet).

Captions:
- Live auto-captions available (auto-generated from our live ASR). Accuracy varies; we can run live captions + a human cleanup pass.
- For guaranteed T+30 delivery we need to schedule a human transcriber in Rev with expedited turnaround (cost add-on). Ops can spin that up for this event, estimate +$350 for 1-2 speakers, +$150 per additional hour of audio.

Attachments: encoder-credentials.txt (this is a stub; do NOT embed keys in public channels).

Sample JS for embed token refresh (very short):
// fetch('/token/refresh?stream=acme-jun9')
// .then(r => r.json()).then(t => player.setAuth(t.jwt));

I’ll coordinate with infra to ensure the captions post-processing job is queued for expedited turnaround on June 9.

Ben Carter
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Chloe/Ben — that all sounds good. A few quick confirms from Acme: 
- We'll use the tokenized iframe approach; my web devs will use the JS helper you mentioned. Please send the sample snippet and a test token when you have it.
- We'll budget for the expedited Rev transcription. Please let us know the sign-up link or PO details.
- Audio reuse: the SOW clause you proposed (30s clip, non-exclusive, 2-year license) is acceptable. We will not require additional talent releases for panelists on our side — we will handle guest permissions where needed.

Attaching our logo pack and the signed sponsor brief — small files, see below. If you can send the encoder credentials stub to our web team (dev@acmeevents.com) that would be helpful.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the mutual action plan.

Oliver
